sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: get_default_marker_environment
tools.description:
Return the default marker environment for the current Python process.
    
    This environment contains metadata about the current Python implementation,
    version, platform, and system information. It is used by package markers
    to evaluate conditional dependencies.
    
    Returns:
        A dictionary containing the default environment variables, e.g.
        {"implementation_name": "cpython", "python_version": "3.11", ...}
    
    Example:
        >>> env = get_default_marker_environment()
        >>> env["python_version"]
        '3.11'

tools.name: evaluate_marker
tools.description:
Evaluate a marker expression against an environment.
    
    A marker expression is a string that evaluates to True or False based on
    the environment variables. This is commonly used in dependency specifications.
    
    Args:
        marker: A marker expression to evaluate, e.g. "python_version >= '3.6'"
        environment: Mapping containing keys and values to override the detected environment
        context: The context in which the marker is evaluated, which influences 
                 what marker names are considered valid. Accepted values are 
                 "metadata" (default), "lock_file", and "requirement"
    
    Returns:
        True if the marker matches the environment, otherwise False
    
    Example:
        >>> evaluate_marker("python_version >= '3.6'", {"python_version": "3.8"})
        True

tools.name: parse_metadata_email
tools.description:
Parse distribution metadata stored as email headers. data: Distribution metadata as email headers, e.g. 'Name: example
Version: 1.0
' -> {'core': {'name': 'example', 'version': '1.0'}, 'unparsed': {}}.

samples.data:
Name: example-package
Version: 1.0.0
Summary: An example package

Name: test-package
Version: 2.0.0
Author: John Doe
Author-Email: john@example.com
Classifier: Development Status :: 4 - Beta
Classifier: Intended Audience :: Developers

Name: multi-value-test
Version: 1.0.0
Home-page: https://example.com
Home-page: https://another-example.com

Name: unicode-test
Version: 1.0.0
Summary: Test with unicode: café

tools.name: create_metadata_from_email
tools.description:
Parse metadata from email headers.
    
    Args:
        data: Email header data containing metadata
        validate: Whether to validate the parsed metadata
        
    Returns:
        Dictionary representation of the metadata
        
    Example:
        >>> create_metadata_from_email('Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: example-package\nVersion: 1.0.0\n', True)
        {'metadata_version': '2.1', 'name': 'example-package', 'version': '1.0.0'}

samples.data:
Metadata-Version: 2.1
Name: example-package
Version: 1.0.0
Summary: An example package

From: sender@example.com
To: recipient@example.com
Subject: Test

Metadata-Version: 2.1
Name: test-package
Version: 0.1.0

tools.name: create_empty_version_range
tools.description: Return an empty version range that accepts no versions. prereleases: whether prereleases should be considered when determining if a version is in the range. -> a dictionary representing the empty version range.

tools.name: create_full_version_range
tools.description: Return a full version range that accepts all versions. admit_arbitrary: whether to admit arbitrary strings as versions; prereleases: whether to include pre-release versions. Example: create_full_version_range() -> 'VersionRange(full)'.

tools.name: create_singleton_version_range
tools.description: Return a version range that only accepts a single specific version. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> '{1.0}'. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions.

tools.name: intersect_version_ranges
tools.description: Compute the intersection of two version ranges. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier. Example: intersect_version_ranges('>=1.0', '<2.0') -> '>=1.0,<2.0'.

tools.name: union_version_ranges
tools.description: Compute the union of two version ranges. version_range_a: First version range in PEP 440 format, version_range_b: Second version range in PEP 440 format. Example: union_version_ranges(">=1.0", "<2.0") -> ">=1.0,<2.0".

tools.name: complement_version_range
tools.description: Compute the complement of a version range. version_range: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet, e.g. '>=1.0' -> '<1.0'.

tools.name: difference_version_ranges
tools.description: Compute the difference between two version ranges. version_range_a: The first version range in specifier format, version_range_b: The second version range in specifier format.

tools.name: check_version_range_subset
tools.description: Check if one version range is a subset of another. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier to check if range1 is a subset of it. >>> check_version_range_subset('>=1.5,<1.8', '>=1.0,<2.0') -> True

tools.name: check_version_range_superset
tools.description: Check if one version range is a superset of another. outer_range: A version range specifier string for the outer range, inner_range: A version range specifier string for the inner range.

tools.name: check_version_ranges_disjoint
tools.description:
Check if two version ranges have no overlapping versions.
    
    Args:
        version_range1 (str): First version range specifier (e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0')
        version_range2 (str): Second version range specifier (e.g., '>=2.0,<3.0')
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the ranges are disjoint (no overlap), False otherwise
        
    Example:
        >>> check_version_ranges_disjoint('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=2.0,<3.0')
        True

tools.name: check_version_in_range
tools.description:
Check if a version is contained within a version range.
    
    :param specifier_set: A specifier set that can be converted to a version range
    :param version: The version string to check against the range
    :return: True if the version is contained in the range, False otherwise
    
    >>> check_version_in_range(">=1.0,<2.0", "1.5")
    True
    >>> check_version_in_range(">=1.0,<2.0", "2.0")
    False

tools.name: check_specifier_set_unsatisfiable
tools.description:
Check whether this specifier set can never be satisfied.
    
    Returns True if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string representation of version specifiers
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the specifier set is unsatisfiable, False otherwise
        
    Example:
        >>> check_specifier_set_unsatisfiable(">=2.0,<1.0")
        True

tools.name: convert_specifier_set_to_range
tools.description: Convert a specifier set to a version range. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'.

tools.name: check_specifier_set_subset
tools.description: Check if one specifier set is a subset of another. specifier_set1: The first specifier set to check. specifier_set2: The second specifier set to check against. >>> check_specifier_set_subset('>=3.12,<3.13', '>=3.12') True

tools.name: check_specifier_set_superset
tools.description: Check if one specifier set is a superset of another. specifier_set1: The first specifier set to check. specifier_set2: The second specifier set to check against. >>> check_specifier_set_superset('>=3.12', '>=3.12,<3.13') True

tools.name: check_specifier_sets_disjoint
tools.description:
Check if two specifier sets have no matching versions.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set1 (str): First specifier set string
        specifier_set2 (str): Second specifier set string
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the sets have no matching versions, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> check_specifier_sets_disjoint("<3.12", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: check_version_in_specifier_set
tools.description: Check if a version is contained within a specifier set. specifier_set: A string representing the version specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1'), version: The version string to check against the specifier set, prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440.

tools.name: generate_generic_tags
tools.description: Generate generic interpreter tags. interpreter: The name of the interpreter, e.g. 'cp39'. abis: Iterable of compatible ABIs, e.g. ['cp39', 'abi3']. platforms: Iterable of compatible platforms, e.g. ['linux_x86_64']. -> List of tag strings like 'cp39-none-linux_x86_64'.
